draft.title: The income statement
card: An income statement reports the revenue and expenses of a business for a period of time, such as a month or a year.
Revenue is the income earned from the services the business provides. Expenses are the costs of running the business in that period, such as wages and rent.
Net profit = revenue - expenses. If expenses are greater than revenue, the business has a net loss.
The income statement shows the result for the period only. It does not list assets or liabilities.
draft.remember: The income statement shows revenue less expenses, which gives the profit or loss for a period.

a.q: Which of these is reported on an income statement?
opts: Fees earned and wages paid in March
The money owed to suppliers on 31 March
The value of the van at 31 March
a.why: Fees earned are revenue and wages paid are an expense, so both belong on the income statement for the period. The other options are amounts at a date, which are not part of this report.
a.clue: Look for the option that covers a period of time.

b.q: Priya runs a dog grooming service in Bendigo. In June she earned $9,000 in fees and had expenses of $9,800. What does her income statement show for June?
b.why: Net profit = revenue - expenses, so $9,000 - $9,800 = -$800. Expenses are greater than revenue, so this is a net loss, not a profit.
b.clue: Take expenses away from revenue and check the sign.

a.best: Fees earned and wages paid in March

problems.detail: The right option is the only one not ending 'at 31 March' and the only one naming two items, so it stands out from the three matching distractors. The clue then points straight to it, so a student could pick it without knowing what an income statement reports.

'Wages paid' describes a cash payment, which belongs on the cash flow statement. The card defines expenses as costs of running the business in the period, so 'wages for March' or 'wages expense' would avoid blurring the income statement with cash flows (point 4, cash and profit).
